prompt: We trained a model that predicts customer churn really well — 92% AUC. The top features by importance are: account_age, last_login_days, support_tickets, and pricing_tier. Marketing wants to know which of these we should actually intervene on to reduce churn. Can I use the feature importances to decide?
assertions: Claude clearly states that feature importance in a predictive model does not imply that intervening on that feature will change the outcome

Claude identifies last_login_days as a downstream indicator — customers stop logging in BECAUSE they are already disengaging, not the other way around — and therefore explicitly states it is NOT a valid intervention target: re-engagement campaigns that move the login metric may not reduce churn because they address the symptom, not the cause. Claude does NOT label it 'potentially actionable' or give it 'medium causal plausibility' without flagging this critical caveat.

Claude explicitly invokes do-operator reasoning: observing P(churn | last_login_days = 30) — the churn rate among users who happen to log in every 30 days — is not the same as P(churn | do(last_login_days = 30)) — what would happen if you forced users to log in every 30 days. The model captures the former; marketing needs the latter.

Claude recommends building a causal DAG and identifying a proper estimation strategy before deciding where to intervene — and does NOT recommend targeting features simply because they have high importance scores
